tasks.short: Design the program, carry out treatment sessions, adjust the program and record it in the treatment plan.

steps.what: Physical therapist designs an individually designed program of physical treatment from the exam findings
Physical therapist carries out treatment sessions with exercise and manual therapy
Physical therapist adjusts the program from session to session
Physical therapist writes the program into the treatment plan

tasks.design: Nothing changes in this task's time. Designing, treating and adjusting stay fully with the therapist, and writing the program into the treatment plan is the therapist's own first write.
tasks.previous_blocker: Nothing blocks a change; the work is the therapist's own.
tasks.still_hard: Each patient needs a program that fits; templates are a start.
tasks.human_edge: Feeling under the hands how a joint responds and changing course.

evidence.claim: Practice records support treatment plan templates with pick lists.
The patient dossier is kept twenty years after the last change.

assumptions: Boundary: from exam findings to the recorded plan; discharge is outside.
Input contract: exam findings recorded by the therapist.
Designing, treating and adjusting do not change.
No AI suggests treatment.
s4 is the therapist's first write of the program in the treatment plan and keeps its full time.
research_questions: Do plans follow the guidelines more often?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: No saving in this task: every step is the therapist's own judgement, treatment or first write.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take the history, perform tests, determine the diagnosis, record the exam and send the report to the referrer.

steps.what: Patient answers history questions about the complaint
Physical therapist takes the patient's history
Physical therapist performs the physical tests of the initial exam
Physical therapist evaluates the data to determine a diagnosis prior to intervention
Physical therapist types the exam into the record: history, test results and diagnosis typed today; after the change history answers are already in the template and test results go into fixed fields
Physical therapist writes the exam report for the referring GP
Physical therapist checks the report before it goes: history, findings, diagnosis and plan match the record, and it goes to the referring GP
Physical therapist sends the checked exam report to the referring GP: by post today, by one release through secure care messaging after the change

tasks.design: Patients fill in a standard intake questionnaire before the first visit, and the answers appear in the exam template in the practice record ({OTHER}), so the therapist asks follow-up questions instead of the full list. Test results go into fixed template fields. Once the therapist has completed the record, the practice record builds the report for the GP from it; the therapist checks it and releases it by secure care messaging. Testing and the diagnosis stay with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: The history was taken question by question and reports were typed and posted.
tasks.enabler_now: Practice records take intake questionnaires and build referrer reports from templates.
tasks.still_hard: Patients answer questionnaires briefly; red flags must still be asked in person.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting the warning sign that means this back pain needs a doctor.

reach.learn: Whether structured reports are read sooner.

evidence.claim: Practice records take intake questionnaires and build referrer reports from templates.
Health data are special category; expect a DPIA.

assumptions: Boundary: from referral to the report sent; treatment is outside.
Input contract: referral from the GP or patient self-referral; intake questionnaire filled in by the patient; templates set by the practice's therapists; fallback is asking in the visit.
Testing and diagnosis do not change.
Patients' time is priced as customer time, not as the therapist's savings.

No new focal work: reading the questionnaire is counted in s1, and learning the template is a one-off, not ongoing work. s4 keeps 75: history answers fill the template, but test results and the diagnosis are the therapist's own first record. s8 keeps its time for the release.
unknowns: Share of patients who fill in the questionnaire.
research_questions: Does the first visit leave more time for testing?

already_counted.description: Physical therapist reads the questionnaire before the visit.

incremental.description: Patients fill in the intake questionnaire before the first visit (part moved from the therapist's history taking).

approvals.approved_version: The exam report exactly as checked by the therapist in s7, sent once by secure care messaging to the referring GP; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: half of patients skip the questionnaire, so s1 and s4 keep 85 (10.8); high: most patients fill it in before the visit (17.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write session notes, enter outcome scores, and update prognosis and goals in the chart.

steps.what: Physical therapist writes treatment and response notes in the patient's chart after each session

loop.input: The recording of the session, made with the patient's consent, and the treatment plan.
loop.output: A draft session note in the practice's template: complaint, treatment given, response and plan.
loop.check: The therapist reads each draft against what happened in the session (treatment given and the patient's response), edits and signs it, and types the note when the draft misses or changes a point; edit time is logged and a monthly sample is audited for omissions.
loop.stop: One draft per session; on failure the therapist types the note.
loop.why_not_simpler: The session is free talk; a template cannot turn it into a note.

steps.what: Patient fills in pain and function questionnaires on paper
Physical therapist enters pain and function questionnaire scores into the record: typed from paper today; after the change only for patients who cannot use the tablet
Physical therapist updates the prognosis and treatment goals

tasks.design: With the patient's consent, a scribe records the session and drafts the note in the practice record ({OTHER}); the therapist edits and signs it. Patients fill in pain and function questionnaires on a tablet, so scores land in the record and chart over time. Updating the prognosis stays with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes were typed after each session and scores copied from paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Scribes draft notes for clinicians to validate, and questionnaires on tablets write scores to the record.
tasks.still_hard: Drafts can omit or invent details; the therapist must read every note.
tasks.human_edge: Writing down what the patient did not say but the therapist saw.
tasks.altitude: The therapist edits and signs drafted notes instead of typing them.

reach.learn: Whether the same scribe works for other therapies.

evidence.claim: Autoscriber records the consultation; the clinician validates; the note goes into the record.
Across 236,153 scribe notes, self-estimated time per note fell from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes (29%); three of seven authors were from the vendor.
Ambient recording captures staff performance, so the works council must consent.
Providers are responsible for careful use of generative AI: assess risks, test and monitor.

assumptions: Boundary: from the session to the updated chart; reports to the GP and treatment decisions are outside.
Input contract: questionnaires filled in by patients on the practice tablet; about 90% of patients can use it, so s2 keeps 10 for typing the rest.
Patients may refuse recording; then the therapist types the note.
Recordings are deleted once the note is signed.
Patients already fill in the questionnaires on paper; the tablet takes about the same time, so no customer time is added.
unknowns: Share of patients who agree to recording.
research_questions: Does note time fall as much as in the published case?

already_counted.description: Physical therapist edits and signs each drafted note.

incremental.description: Physical therapist asks for recording consent.
Practice owner audits a monthly sample of notes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: half of patients refuse recording, so s1 keeps 85, and half of questionnaires stay on paper, so s2 keeps 50 (19.4); high: most consent and 90% use the tablet (37.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Demonstrate home exercises, watch the patient practise, select exercises with videos, send the home program and answer questions.

steps.what: Physical therapist instructs patient and family in treatment procedures to be continued at home
Physical therapist watches the patient practise and corrects technique
Physical therapist draws exercises and doses on paper handouts
Physical therapist checks the final home program: exercises, repetitions and frequency match what the patient practised, and it goes to this patient
Physical therapist gives the checked home program to the patient: as a printed handout today, by one release in the home exercise app after the change
Physical therapist answers patients' questions about the home program by phone

tasks.design: The therapist picks exercises from a video library in a home exercise app ({OTHER}) and sets repetitions and frequency, instead of drawing them; the therapist checks the program and releases it to the patient with the videos. Demonstrating, correcting and answering questions stay with the therapist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Exercises were drawn on paper handouts that patients lost or misread.
tasks.enabler_now: Home exercise apps hold video libraries and send programs to patients.
tasks.still_hard: Videos show the movement, not this patient's mistakes.
tasks.human_edge: Showing a nervous family member how to help without hurting.

evidence.claim: Home exercise apps hold video libraries and send programs to patients.
Health data are special category; the app needs a processing agreement.

assumptions: Boundary: from instruction to questions answered; progress review is outside.
Input contract: treatment program from the therapist's plan; video library from the app supplier, checked by the practice's therapists; fallback is paper handouts.
Instruction and correction do not change.
Patients without a phone get a printout.
s3 keeps 40 for choosing exercises and setting doses; drawing them goes. s4 keeps 10 for the release.
unknowns: Share of patients who use the app.
research_questions: Do patients do more of their home exercises?

incremental.description: Physical therapist helps patients install the app.

approvals.approved_version: The home program with exercises, repetitions and frequency exactly as checked by the therapist in s3b, sent once to this patient through the home exercise app; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the library lacks many of the exercises used, so s3 keeps 70, and many patients need a printout, so s4 keeps 60 (5.2); high: the library covers most exercises and most patients use the app (11.9).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The physical therapist keeps examining, treating and teaching; typing notes, scores, reports and handouts shrinks.
role.ambitious_version: A therapist who finishes notes before the next patient walks in.
